tape-classic: Tape-In Hair Extensions, also known as tape hair extensions, is a popular hair extension technology widely used in the US and Europe. The main advantage of this technique is an even distribution of load on your natural hair: hair is attached with a wide tape rather than small individual strands, as with bonded extensions.

Tape-in extensions significantly cut down the procedure time, and with the right colour and density match the thin tapes look natural. You don't need to sacrifice your own length — with correct installation and care, Tape-In lets your natural hair grow out undisturbed.
Quality tapes are designed for repeated use and, with correct care, can last a year or longer. Choose quality hair and materials once — and get an extension system you can use again and again.
tape-imitation-1: Tape-In with root imitation is an enhanced version of classic tape-in extensions. The underlying technology stays the same: hair is attached with a wide tape that spreads the load evenly across your natural hair. In addition, a root imitation is used, which makes the attachment point less noticeable.
Imitation 1.0 is a classic tape with an added root imitation. It makes the attachment less noticeable, though on close inspection a small strip of tape — about 2 mm — may be visible.
It's a great option for those who want a more natural look at the roots, plus extra volume and length, while keeping the affordable price and convenience of classic Tape-In.
tape-imitation-2: Tape-In with root imitation is an enhanced version of classic tape-in extensions. The underlying technology stays the same: hair is attached with a wide tape that spreads the load evenly across your natural hair. In addition, a root imitation is used, which makes the attachment point less noticeable.
Imitation 2.0 is a more advanced version: the hair is hand-stitched strand by strand, creating the most natural possible attachment. In Imitation 2.0, the tape itself is not visible at all.
This option is especially valued by those for whom maximum discretion, a natural parting, and the feeling that the hair grows directly from the scalp matter most.

selfCorrection.title: Self-correction
selfCorrection.description: Once you've learned the technique in a course, the tapes can be repositioned yourself at home. You don't have to visit a stylist every time — you just need the right materials and to follow the method strictly.
selfCorrection.warningText: Below is a general sequence of correction steps, not a complete protocol. The exact list of materials and step-by-step method is taught in the training course — self-correction without training, or with the method not followed, can damage your natural hair.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.description: Gather the materials for removing and reinstalling the tape, and wash and dry your hair without oils or conditioners near the roots.

steps.title: Removing the old tape
steps.description: Carefully dissolve the adhesive with a tape remover, without pulling or forcefully combing the strands.

steps.title: Preparing the strand
steps.description: Section off a strand the same width as the tape, and clean any adhesive residue from the roots.

steps.title: Installing the new tape
steps.description: Firmly and evenly attach the tape at the root, following the technique learned in training.

steps.title: Check
steps.description: Make sure the tape sits evenly and doesn't pinch your natural hair, adjusting if needed.
